title: StratoAccel partner intro & integration discovery
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and Stratosphere Accelerator Systems to explore a technical+commercial partnership. Covered Stratosphere's GPU appliance portfolio, software stack (driver/kernel compatibility, Triton/ONNX support), potential integration points with Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments, security/compliance requirements (KMS, SSO, SOC2), and initial PoC scope and timelines. Action items include sharing integration guide, scheduling a bench run on Stratosphere A100/RTX nodes, and a follow-up technical deep-dive focused on private deploy networking.
topics: Redwood Dedicated vs Private deployment fit
security: KMS, SSO, audit logs, SOC 2
PoC scope: performance bench + validation suite
action_items: Jordan Lee - Send partner-integration-deck and joint GTM one-pager - due 2026-05-12
Priya Desai - Share detailed runtime compatibility checklist (kernels, cuDNN, Triton config) - due 2026-05-14
Evan Park - Provide SSH access to two lab nodes and sample model artifacts for bench run - target 2026-05-13
Lena Müller - Share security questionnaire + redacted SOC2 report - due 2026-05-11
next_steps: Schedule 90m deep-dive on private deployment and network architecture (Redwood SE + Stratosphere infra) - proposed week of 2026-05-18
Run initial perf bench on A100 and RTX-6000 hardware with Redwood's small benchmark (benchmarks.csv) and share results
Circulate commercial term sketch for reseller pilot after bench completes
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-07 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Redwood Solutions Eng), Maya Chen (Redwood Partnerships) — Marta Kovács (Stratosphere, Head of Partnerships), Evan Park (GPU SW Lead), Sanjay Rao (Cloud Integration PM), Lena Müller (Security & Compliance)
Links referenced: partner-integration-deck (drive link), benchmarks.csv (sheet), security-pack.pdf (secure link)

Summary section (auto): quick intros, product/stack overview from Stratosphere, compatibility and PoC logistics discussed, security ask listed, next steps agreed.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on the partnerships team. Quick round robin?
[00:06] Marta: Hi I'm Marta, head of partnerships at Stratosphere, uh we build the accelerator appliances and channel programs. Happy to be here.
[00:12] Evan: Evan Park, GPU software lead — I handle drivers, runtimes, and the SW distro we ship on the boxes.
[00:18] Sanjay: Sanjay Rao, cloud integration PM, focus on networking stories and orchestration.
[00:22] Lena: Lena Müller, security & compliance, I own SOC 2 and customer audits.
[00:26] Priya: Priya Desai, Redwood SE, I'll lead technical integration conversations.
[00:30] Tom: Tom Alvarez, solutions eng — doing partner enablement stuff.
[00:34] Jordan: Cool, agenda: quick intro from both sides, hardware and runtime details, where Redwood fits (hosted/dedicated/private options), security asks, and propose a PoC + next steps. Anything else?
[00:44] Marta: No that's good. We're primarily exploring two things — 1) joint go-to-market where we resell Redwood on our appliances, and 2) technical integration so Redwood can validate low-latency inference on our nodes.
[00:55] Jordan: Makes sense. Priya, quick overview of where Redwood typically sits.
[00:58] Priya: Sure — Redwood provides a unified inference runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. For partners like you, we usually evaluate both Dedicated (reserved capacity on our infra) and Private (customer-managed VPC or on-prem) — for appliances, Private makes sense because you want the control and data isolation. We care about kernel compatibility, quantization pipelines, KV cache behavior, and batching controls.
[01:20] Evan: When you say kernel compatibility — are you looking at CUDA/cuDNN versions, or also our in-house kernel patches?
[01:27] Priya: Both. Ideally we get your exact CUDA/cuDNN/hypervisor stack and any kernel modules. We have an automated compatibility checklist — I'll share that. Sometimes the vendor patches change LSMs or memory mappings and that affects our memory allocator.
[01:40] Evan: Right, we recently shipped an updated stack for A100 GenX and RTX-6000 where we tweak GPU page pinning. Might need to test with Redwood's allocator.
[01:50] Jordan: High level commercial question — do you foresee us buying hardware from Stratosphere, or you reselling Redwood's software with the appliance? Marta?
[01:58] Marta: We want both options on the table. A joint pilot where our channel sells the appliance bundled with Redwood private runtime would be ideal. We also want a performance stamp for marketing.
[02:08] Tom: For the stamp, we typically run a small benchmark on typical LLM workloads. Benchmarks should include token latency p95, throughput at batch sizes 1, 4, 16, and cost per token estimate.
[02:20] Sanjay: On networking — our appliances usually sit behind an on-prem load balancer and NAT to customer subnets. How does Redwood Private expect inbound/outbound?
[02:29] Priya: For Private deployments, we support a customer-controlled control plane or a light-weight outbound-only management channel. If you need total air-gap, we also have an on-prem package. The main networking requirement is consistent outbound to the control plane for metrics and rollouts, unless you want full self-hosted control plane.
[02:45] Lena: On security, SOC 2 is key for our customers. We also require KMS integration for key management and detailed audit logs. Can Redwood integrate with our HSM/KMS?
[02:55] Jordan: Yes, Redwood supports KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, GCP KMS) and we have HSM integrations for private installs. We'll need to confirm HSM vendor specifics though.
[03:05] Lena: We'll share the list. Also SSO/SAML for portal and token management — do you have RBAC?
[03:11] Priya: Yes RBAC and SAML/SCIM, plus token scoping. We'll share our security pack.
[03:16] Marta: What's typical PoC length and success criteria?
[03:20] Jordan: For HW+SW validation, we usually do a 2-4 week bench pilot: 1 week environment setup, 1-2 weeks benchmarking and tweaks, and wrap-up with a joint tech review. Success criteria: p95 latency target, throughput within X% of cloud baseline, and no functional regressions on quantized models.
[03:36] Evan: I'd like to run a quick sanity bench on one of our A100 nodes. We'll need the sample model and a small harness. Do you provide that?
[03:43] Priya: Yes, we have a compact bench harness (we call it small-bench) and a sample 7B model artifact. We'll push it as a tarball; ideally we get access to two lab nodes via SSH.
[03:52] Sanjay: We can stand up the nodes, but let's clarify network access and credentials. We prefer short-lived SSH keys and jump hosts.
[03:59] Tom: Noted — Evan, can you create an internal ticket to prepare two nodes and a jump host?
[04:03] Evan: Yeah, I'll do that.
[04:05] (brief crosstalk)
[04:10] Speaker 2: sorry — quick question on quantization: do you support 4-bit patching and int8?
[04:15] Priya: We support a number of quantization profiles (int8, 4-bit LLMQ, some mixed-bit modes). There's occasionally model-specific accuracy tradeoffs; we'll want to run the eval set.
[04:26] Marta: On go-to-market, we wanted to understand pricing flexibility for bundled resells and any channel discounts.
[04:32] Jordan: For pilots we can offer a partner pilot credit and a reseller discount baseline. Commercial details we usually sketch after a successful bench — we can share a commercial sketch next steps.
[04:42] Lena: Also compliance — we need to make sure audit logs and retention can meet enterprise requirements, e.g., 1 year retention and exportable CSVs.
[04:51] Priya: We have per-token cost and telemetry retention controls in the console; logs can be exported and we can adjust retention windows for enterprise customers.
[04:59] Evan: A technical note — some of our boxes run a custom hypervisor for live-migration; will Redwood's runtime support that? We had odd behaviors with KV cache invalidation in similar setups.
[05:10] Priya: That's exactly the kind of thing we want to test. KV cache (we sometimes call it kev cache in notes — hah) and prefix caching can interact badly with live migration. We'll add live-migration scenarios to the bench plans.
[05:22] Jordan: Great. Timeline — can we aim to have the bench spun up week of May 11th?
[05:26] Evan: Tentatively yes, pending node prep.
[05:30] Marta: We'll also want co-branded case study language ready after a successful pilot.
[05:35] Maya: From Redwood Partnerships POV we'll draft a co-marketing plan and partner enablement checklist.
[05:41] Sanjay: On the deep technical side, I'd like a follow-up to discuss network topology — whether we use outbound-only control plane or self-hosted control plane. Also how model bits are fetched and cached.
[05:50] Priya: We'll schedule a 90-minute deep-dive with our infra folks. Proposed week of May 18th.
[05:56] Jordan: To wrap — action items and owners: Priya will share compatibility checklist and bench harness; Jordan will send partner-integration-deck and a commercial sketch; Evan will stand up two lab nodes and provide access; Lena will send security questionnaire and a redacted SOC2; Marta will coordinate commercial introductions. Anything else?
[06:18] Lena: We'll also review data residency requirements — some customers require EU-only logs. We'll send a note on that.
[06:25] Jordan: Perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invites and links to the repo/sheet. Thanks everyone.
[06:30] Marta: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
